guide.summary: Forgejo documents OAuth2 Authorization Code with PKCE for connecting an app to a user's own instance. OAuth2 scopes are not implemented, so the token acts with the user's full permissions, and the app must enforce read-only behavior.
guide.recommendation: The requested API test is not ready yet. Resolve the access mapping for List repository names visible to the connected person, including pagination. Use “Find missing request” or add official documentation beside that action.

findings.title: Forgejo documents OAuth2 provider flow with authorization code and PKCE
findings.detail: Forgejo acts as an OAuth2 provider, with authorization, token, and userinfo endpoints. Supported grant is Authorization Code with PKCE extension. Public and confidential client types are supported.
findings.appliesWhen: Customer connects an individual account on their own Forgejo instance using OAuth

evidence.quote: OAuth2 provider Forgejo supports acting as an OAuth2 provider to allow third party applications to access its resources with the user’s consent.
Authorization Endpoint /login/oauth/authorize Access Token Endpoint /login/oauth/access_token
Supported OAuth2 Grants At the moment, Forgejo only supports the Authorization Code Grant standard with additional support for the following extensions:

findings.title: OAuth2 scopes are not implemented, so tokens act with full user rights
findings.detail: Scopes are not implemented for OAuth2 tokens and they can be used to execute any actions on behalf of the user. Scoped access tokens are a different mechanism. The read-only use case must be enforced by the app, not by a token scope.
findings.appliesWhen: Any OAuth connection to the user's Forgejo instance

evidence.quote: OAuth2 scopes are not yet implemented.
Note Scopes are not implemented for OAuth2 tokens and they can be used to
execute any actions on behalf of the user, not just Git-related actions.

findings.title: Register an OAuth application on the customer's instance before testing
findings.detail: Registration happens in user settings applications. Confidential clients receive a client ID and secret, and PKCE public clients must be registered as public. The redirect URI must match exactly between authorize and token requests.

evidence.quote: OpenID Connect (OIDC) To use the Authorization Code Grant as a third-party application, it is required to register a new application via the “Settings” ( /user/settings/applications ) section. To test
The REDIRECT_URI in the access_token request must match the REDIRECT_URI in the authorize request.
Note Please ensure you have registered your OAuth application as a public client.

findings.title: Send OAuth access token as Bearer header to the API
findings.detail: OAuth access tokens are accepted with an Authorization Bearer header. The instance base URL is a per-customer input used to build the token and API URLs.
findings.appliesWhen: Each API call after the token exchange

evidence.quote: OAuth2 Provider Access tokens obtained from Forgejo’s OAuth2 provider are accepted by these methods:
Authorization: Bearer ... header in HTTP headers
Use the access_token to make API requests to access the user’s resources.

findings.title: Use page and limit parameters for pagination
findings.detail: The API supports pagination with page and limit parameters. Link headers and x-total-count are returned when results span multiple pages.

evidence.quote: Pagination The API supports pagination. The page and limit parameters are used to specify the page number and the number of items per page. As well, the Link header is
returned with the next, previous, and last page links if there are more than one page. The x-total-count is also returned to indicate the total number of items.
Parameter page in query (integer, optional): page number of results to return (1-based) Schema: {"type":"integer"}

steps.title: Register a public OAuth2 application on the customer's Forgejo instance
steps.detail: Using the customer's own account on their instance, create an OAuth2 application at /user/settings/applications as a public client with a single redirect URI. Record the Client ID. No client secret is used for the PKCE public client path.
steps.doneWhen: The application exists, is registered as a public client, and its Client ID and the exact redirect URI are recorded.

evidence.quote: Note Please ensure you have registered your OAuth application as a public client.

OpenID Connect (OIDC) To use the Authorization Code Grant as a third-party application, it is required to register a new application via the “Settings” ( /user/settings/applications ) section. To test
The REDIRECT_URI in the access_token request must match the REDIRECT_URI in the authorize request.

fields: INSTANCE_BASE_URL: customer's HTTPS Forgejo origin, supplied by customer
REDIRECT_URI: the app's callback URL, must match exactly in later requests

steps.title: Generate PKCE code_verifier and S256 code_challenge
steps.detail: Create a random code_verifier of 43 to 128 characters using alphanumerics and - . _ ~. Derive code_challenge as URL-safe base64 of the SHA256 hash of the verifier, and generate a random STATE value.
steps.doneWhen: CODE_VERIFIER, CODE_CHALLENGE and STATE are stored for the single authorization attempt.

evidence.quote: To achieve this, you have to provide a code_verifier for every authorization request. A code_verifier has to be a random string with a minimum length of 43 characters and a
If you have the required functionality on your client, set code_challenge to be a URL-safe base64-encoded string of the SHA256 hash of code_verifier . In that case, your code_challenge_method becomes

https://[ YOUR-FORGEJO-URL ]/login/oauth/authorize?client_id=CLIENT_ID&redirect_uri=REDIRECT_URI&response_type=code&code_challenge_method=CODE_CHALLENGE_METHOD&code_challenge=CODE_CHALLENGE&state=STATE The CLIENT_ID can be obtained by registering an

fields: CODE_VERIFIER: generated locally, kept secret
CODE_CHALLENGE: derived from CODE_VERIFIER with S256
STATE: random value checked on callback

steps.title: Obtain the user's consent and check the callback
steps.detail: Open the authorization URL in a browser as the customer user. After consent, the browser redirects to REDIRECT_URI with code and state. Verify the returned state equals the generated STATE before exchanging the code.
steps.doneWhen: The callback returns a code and the returned state matches the generated STATE. This is a manual consent step; nothing has been executed by the agent.

steps.title: Exchange the authorization code for an access token
steps.detail: POST the code with grant_type authorization_code, the redirect_uri, client_id and the PKCE code_verifier to the documented token endpoint. Read access_token from the JSON response.
steps.doneWhen: The response contains an access_token with token_type bearer. The token is stored only for later read calls.

steps.title: List repositories visible to the user, first page
steps.detail: Call GET /api/v1/repos/search with limit and page=1. Read repository names from $.data[].name. Boundary check: the OAuth token has no scope and grants full user rights, so the app must enforce read-only use; confirm the outgoing request log contains only GET requests and no create, edit or delete calls. Visible-repository completeness is unresolved because the documented search needs a keyword-free mode that is not shown.
steps.doneWhen: The first page returns 200 with a data array and the Link and x-total-count headers are inspected for a rel=next link. Boundary check: confirm only GET requests were sent and no repository was created, edited or deleted.

evidence.quote: Response JSON paths for GET /api/v1/repos/search: $.data[].name (string)
Pagination The API supports pagination. The page and limit parameters are used to specify the page number and the number of items per page. As well, the Link header is
returned with the next, previous, and last page links if there are more than one page. The x-total-count is also returned to indicate the total number of items.

fields: ACCESS_TOKEN: from exchange-authorization-code
INSTANCE_BASE_URL: your full HTTPS instance URL, without a trailing slash

steps.title: List repositories visible to the user, continuation page
steps.detail: Repeat the same search with page=2 and the same limit, preserving the original query parameters. Continue until the Link header has no rel=next link or the page is empty; x-total-count may be used to confirm the total.
steps.doneWhen: The continuation response is read and the end condition (no rel=next link) is confirmed. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

blockers.title: OAuth tokens have no scope restriction
blockers.resolution: The app must itself enforce read-only behavior, since the token can perform any action the user can. Do not call write endpoints.

blockers.title: List repository names visible to the connected person, including pagination
